q: The minimum cover for direct-buried UF cable (general case, not under a building or slab) is:
explain: Direct-burial cables: 24 in. RMC/IMC: 6 in. Nonmetallic raceways without concrete: 18 in. Residential 120 V, 20 A GFCI-protected branch circuits: 12 in.

q: Minimum cover for rigid metal conduit (RMC) or IMC buried in earth is:
explain: 6 in. for RMC and IMC. Under a 4-in. slab with no vehicle traffic, cover can be reduced further per the table.

q: Minimum cover for rigid PVC conduit buried in earth without a concrete envelope is:
explain: 18 in. for nonmetallic raceways listed for direct burial without concrete encasement.

q: A cable run through bored holes in wood studs must have the edge of the hole at least how far from the nearest edge of the framing member, or be protected by a steel plate?
explain: 1¼ in.; otherwise a steel plate or bushing at least 1/16 in. thick is required.

q: At each outlet, junction, or switch point, at least how much free conductor must be left for splices or device connections?
explain: 6 in. measured from where the conductor emerges from the raceway or sheath, and extending at least 3 in. outside a box opening smaller than 8 in.

q: The ampacity of 3/0 AWG copper THWN (75°C column) is:
The ampacity of 6 AWG copper at 75°C is:
explain: Copper 75°C: 8 AWG → 50 A, 6 AWG → 65 A, 4 AWG → 85 A, 3 AWG → 100 A, 2 AWG → 115 A, 1 AWG → 130 A.

q: Eight current-carrying conductors are installed in one raceway. The ampacity adjustment factor is:
Nine 12 AWG THHN copper current-carrying conductors share one conduit at 30°C. What is the adjusted ampacity, and what is the largest OCPD generally permitted?
explain: Start at the 90°C column (30 A) × 70% = 21 A. The small-conductor rule still caps 12 AWG copper at a 20 A device.

q: The temperature correction factor for a 90°C-rated conductor in a 45°C ambient is:
explain: 90°C column: 36–40°C → 0.91; 41–45°C → 0.87; 46–50°C → 0.82. Always start from the conductor's own temperature column.

q: Conductors may generally be connected in parallel only in sizes:
explain: 1/0 AWG and larger, with each set matching in length, material, size, insulation and termination method.

q: Using the 83% rule for a one-family dwelling, the minimum copper conductor size for a 200 A service is:
explain: 200 A × 0.83 = 166 A → 2/0 Cu (175 A at 75°C). Table 310.12 lists 2/0 Cu or 4/0 Al for 200 A.

q: For box-fill calculations, each 12 AWG conductor is counted at:
explain: 14 AWG → 2.00; 12 AWG → 2.25; 10 AWG → 2.50; 8 AWG → 3.00; 6 AWG → 5.00 cubic inches.

q: A device box contains four 12 AWG circuit conductors, two 12 AWG equipment grounding conductors, one duplex receptacle, and no internal clamps. Minimum box volume?
explain: 4 conductors + 1 (all EGCs together) + 2 (device yoke) = 7 volumes × 2.25 in³ = 15.75 in³.

q: For a straight pull of 4 AWG or larger conductors, the length of the pull box shall be at least how many times the trade size of the largest raceway?
explain: Straight pulls: 8× the largest raceway. Angle/U pulls: 6× the largest plus the sum of other raceways in the same row on that wall.

q: A pull box has one 3-in. and two 2-in. conduits entering the same wall for an angle pull. The minimum distance from that wall to the opposite wall is:
explain: 6 × 3 in. = 18 in., plus the other raceways on that wall (2 + 2) = 22 in.

q: The maximum fill for a raceway containing more than two conductors is:
explain: One conductor → 53%; two → 31%; more than two → 40%.

q: A conduit nipple not over 24 in. long between boxes may be filled to:
explain: 60% fill for nipples 24 in. or less, and the ampacity adjustment factors of 310.15(C) do not apply to them.

q: EMT must be securely fastened within how far of each box or termination, and supported at intervals not exceeding how far?
explain: Within 3 ft of each termination and every 10 ft. RMC and IMC share the 3 ft / 10 ft baseline.

q: Flexible metal conduit must be secured within how far of each box and at intervals not exceeding:
explain: Within 12 in. of terminations and every 4½ ft. Unsecured lengths up to 3 ft (6 ft for luminaire whips) are allowed where flexibility is needed.

q: Type NM cable must be secured within how far of every box and supported at intervals not exceeding:
explain: Within 12 in. of boxes and every 4½ ft. Horizontal runs through framing holes count as supported.

q: Type NM cable with 90°C conductors: what ampacity column may be used for the final ampacity?
explain: The 90°C rating may be used for adjustment and correction, but the final ampacity cannot exceed the 60°C column (12 AWG NM → 20 A).

q: Expansion fittings are required for rigid PVC conduit where the expected length change due to temperature is at least:
explain: ¼ in. or more in a straight run between securely mounted items. Table 352.44 gives the expansion per 100 ft.

q: Generally, raceways shall NOT be used as a means of support for:
choices: Other raceways, cables, or nonelectrical equipment
explain: A raceway can't carry other raceways or cables unless identified for the purpose or used to support Class 2 circuit conductors to the equipment the raceway serves.

q: All conductors of the same circuit, including the grounded conductor and equipment grounding conductors, shall generally be:
choices: Run in separate raceways to reduce heating
Contained within the same raceway, cable, or trench
Run with no more than two per raceway
explain: Keeping all circuit conductors together prevents inductive heating of metal raceways and keeps the fault-return path low-impedance.

q: A residential 120 V, 20 A branch circuit with GFCI protection, in direct-burial UF cable, requires a minimum cover of:
explain: 12 in. for residential branch circuits rated 120 V or less, 20 A or less, with GFCI protection.

q: A cable run parallel to a framing member must be kept at least how far from the nearest edge of the member, or be protected?
explain: Same 1¼-in. setback as bored holes, to keep nails and screws out of the cable.

q: Flexible cords and cables shall NOT be used:
choices: As a substitute for the fixed wiring of a structure or run through walls, ceilings, or floors
explain: 400.12 lists prohibited uses: substituting for fixed wiring, through holes in walls/ceilings/floors, through doorways or windows, attached to building surfaces, concealed, etc.

q: How many 12 AWG THHN conductors are permitted in ¾-in. EMT?
explain: Annex C Table C.1 (EMT): ¾ in. → 22 × 14 AWG, 16 × 12 AWG, 10 × 10 AWG THHN. Use Tables 4 and 5 when conductor sizes are mixed.

q: How many 10 AWG THHN conductors are permitted in 1-in. EMT?
explain: Annex C Table C.1: 1-in. EMT holds 16 × 10 AWG THHN (26 × 12 AWG, 35 × 14 AWG).

q: Boxes and conduit bodies shall be installed so the wiring inside:
choices: Can be rendered accessible without removing any part of the building or digging
Can only be reached by the utility
explain: Accessible without damaging the building finish. Listed boxes in underground installations may be covered by gravel or light aggregate if their location is marked.

q: What is the 75°C ampacity of 250 kcmil copper?
Which conductor is generally NOT counted as a current-carrying conductor for ampacity adjustment?
choices: The neutral of a 2-wire 120 V circuit
An ungrounded conductor of a 3-phase circuit
The neutral of a 3-wire circuit supplying nonlinear loads
explain: EGCs never count (310.15(E)). A neutral carrying only unbalanced current of a balanced circuit is not counted (310.15(E)(1)), but a 2-wire circuit's neutral and a nonlinear-load neutral do count.

q: Rigid metal conduit must be secured within how far of each box, cabinet, or conduit body?
explain: Within 3 ft of terminations (5 ft where structural members don't allow 3 ft), and supported every 10 ft; longer spans are allowed for straight runs with threaded couplings per Table 344.30(B)(2).
